intent: Fix the bokehjs DatePicker showing the day before the selected date for users in UTC+ timezones (issue #9129) by shifting the incoming Date by the browser's timezone offset in DatePickerView._unlocal_date, so the user-specified date is recreated regardless of the local timezone. Also adds the first Selenium integration tests for the widget. It must not regress other timezones or the value / min_date / max_date supplied from Python.

findings.title: UTC- browsers show Python-supplied dates one day early
findings.suggested_fix: Stop applying one conversion to both encodings of the model value. Pass the raw model value to the helper and branch on its type: for a number (Python-serialized epoch ms of the calendar date at UTC midnight) use `const d = new Date(v); return new Date(d.getUTCFullYear(), d.getUTCMonth(), d.getUTCDate())` (equivalent to the pre-change toISOString path); for a string written by _on_select's toDateString() use `const d = new Date(v); return new Date(d.getFullYear(), d.getMonth(), d.getDate())` (it already parses as local midnight). Drop the getTimezoneOffset/setTime lines. Assumption: strings on the model are toDateString-style and parse as local time; an ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' string set from JS parses as UTC and should take the UTC branch. A scratch Node run of this shape returned Sep 20 / Sep 1 / Sep 16 for 1568937600000 / 1567296000000 / 'Mon Sep 16 2019' under UTC, Europe/Paris, Pacific/Kiritimati, America/Los_Angeles and Pacific/Pago_Pago.
findings.why_it_matters: A user in any negative-UTC-offset timezone (all of the Americas) who opens DatePicker(value=date(2019, 9, 20), min_date=date(2019, 9, 1), max_date=date(2019, 9, 30)) now sees Sep 19 preselected, can pick Aug 31, and cannot pick Sep 30; before this change those users saw the right dates. The model value has two encodings: epoch ms of UTC midnight when it comes from Python, and a local-midnight toDateString() string after a pick. The offset shift is right only for the string, so the change moves the off-by-one from UTC+ after a pick to UTC- on every Python-supplied value instead of removing it. Branching on the encoding (UTC fields for numbers, local fields for strings) is correct in every timezone.
evidence: bokehjs/src/lib/models/widgets/date_picker.ts:82 -- const timeOffsetInMS = date.getTimezoneOffset() * 60000 (getTimezoneOffset() is positive for UTC- zones, so line 83 moves the instant backwards across UTC midnight)

Callers: date_picker.ts:68 `defaultDate: this._unlocal_date(new Date(this.model.value))`, :70 minDate, :71 maxDate -- all three Python-supplied values pass through the changed function, and connect_signals (:54) re-renders on every model change, so a server callback assigning dp.value hits it again.

Python side: bokeh/util/serialization.py:184 `return (dt.datetime(*obj.timetuple()[:6]) - DT_EPOCH).total_seconds() * 1000` (and :179 for datetime), DT_EPOCH = dt.datetime.utcfromtimestamp(0) at :83, reached from bokeh/core/json_encoder.py:185-186. date(2019, 9, 20) is sent as 1568937600000 = 2019-09-20T00:00:00Z.

Scratch Node run by the orchestrator (copies of the old and new function bodies, TZ set per run): 1568937600000 -> old=Fri Sep 20 / new=Thu Sep 19 under America/Los_Angeles, America/New_York and America/Sao_Paulo; old and new both Fri Sep 20 under UTC, Europe/Paris, Asia/Kolkata and Pacific/Auckland.

Same run, the case the PR does fix: 'Mon Sep 16 2019' (what _on_select stores at date_picker.ts:95) -> old=Sun Sep 15 / new=Mon Sep 16 under Europe/Paris, Asia/Kolkata and Pacific/Auckland; unchanged and correct in the UTC- zones.

Adversarial reviewer's scratch run: min_date 1567296000000 old=Sun Sep 01 / new=Sat Aug 31 and max_date 1569801600000 old=Mon Sep 30 / new=Sun Sep 29 in UTC- zones; a Python datetime with a time of day also regresses for UTC+ users (datetime(2019,9,20,22,30) old=Fri Sep 20 / new=Sat Sep 21 in Europe/Paris).
date_picker.ts:81 -- the new comment claims the result is 'agnostic to their local systems's timezone', which the runs above contradict.

findings.title: New Selenium tests cannot detect the bug or the regression
findings.suggested_fix: Before the first click in test_js_on_change_executes (and in test_basic), assert the initial display: `assert page.driver.find_element_by_css_selector('.foo input').get_attribute('value') == 'Fri Sep 20 2019'`. Then exercise non-zero offsets: either launch the headless Chrome driver with a TZ environment variable for one UTC+ and one UTC- zone (assumption: Chrome on the CI image takes its zone from TZ at launch, not verifiable offline), or add a bokehjs unit test that feeds 1568937600000 and 'Mon Sep 16 2019' through the conversion under TZ=Europe/Paris and TZ=America/Los_Angeles and expects Sep 20 / Sep 16. Replace max_date=datetime.utcnow() with a fixed date so the fixture is not clock-dependent.
findings.why_it_matters: The three new tests are the only verification of this timezone fix, yet with a zero browser offset the changed lines are a no-op, so the tests pass with or without the fix on a UTC runner. They also stay green in every timezone while UTC- users see the initial date one day early, because no assertion reads the input before the click and nothing pins the browser timezone. Asserting the pre-click field value and running the conversion under one UTC+ and one UTC- zone would make the tests fail for both the original bug and the regression in finding 1.
evidence: tests/integration/widgets/test_datepicker.py:65 `assert results['value'] == 'Mon Sep 16 2019'` and :95-98 are the only other value assertions; all come after clicking button[data-pika-day="16"], and none reads the field while it still shows the Python-supplied value=datetime(2019, 9, 20) (:43, :53, :78).
tests/integration/widgets/test_datepicker.py:96 `assert d0.timetuple()[:3] == (2019, 9, 20)` checks `old` as held by the Python model in the server callback; it never passes through _unlocal_date.
Scratch Node run, TZ=UTC: old and new function bodies return the same date for the epoch-ms value and for 'Mon Sep 16 2019', so the assertions at :65/:68 also hold on the base commit there.

Scratch Node run, TZ=America/Los_Angeles: the new function returns Mon Sep 16 for 'Mon Sep 16 2019' (assertions hold) while returning Thu Sep 19 for the initial 1568937600000; no assertion observes it.

No timezone pinning found in the harness: bokeh/_testing/plugins/selenium.py builds Chrome options with only --headless, --no-sandbox and --window-size, and a search of .travis.yml, scripts/ci, tests/integration/conftest.py and bokeh/_testing for TZ/timezone settings found none. Which zone CI runs in was not confirmed from the repo.

residual_risks: adversarial: Pikaday's source is not installed in this environment (bokehjs/package.json:88 pins a git fork), so its handling of defaultDate / setDefaultDate / minDate / maxDate was not read. If its constructor fires onSelect when applying a default date, the day-early value would be written back to the model and, in a server app, to Python without any user action; not verified either way.

adversarial: Python does not re-check a picked value against min_date / max_date (bokeh/models/widgets/inputs.py declares three independent Date properties), so with min_date shifted a day early for UTC- browsers a server callback can receive a date below the configured minimum. Whether downstream app code relies on that bound is outside the reviewed tree.

correctness: the timezone behaviour was established by reading the source and running scratch Node replicas of the old and new function bodies, not by running the widget in a browser; the project build, the Selenium suite and a browser were unavailable, so the three new tests were not executed.
testing_gaps: No test reads the initially displayed date (the Python-supplied value rendered through the changed function), in any timezone.
No test runs the conversion under a non-zero browser offset, so neither the original UTC+ bug nor the UTC- regression can fail the suite.
No test covers a value pushed from Python after first render (server callback assigning dp.value = date(...)): the client receives epoch ms again and re-renders through the changed function.
No test checks that min_date / max_date bound the selectable days (the day before min_date disabled, max_date itself selectable); the changed function shifts both bounds for UTC- browsers.
